environmentRemediation.symptom: PlayMode attempts run-20260914T1 and run-20260914T2 both aborted with 'Aborting batchmode due to failure: Scripts have compiler errors.' - 630 x CS0103 'The name Unsafe does not exist in the current context' inside Library/PackageCache/com.unity.pipeline@9bb4172c603c/Runtime/IlInterpreter/HostBinding.cs and VmEngine.cs, plus the same error in the package's other Runtime/IlInterpreter sources. Zero compiler errors were reported in any ChooGuard assembly in either attempt.
diagnosis: Packages/io.livekit.livekit-sdk/Runtime/Plugins/System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.dll.meta declares isExplicitlyReferenced: 1, so that managed plugin is NOT auto-referenced by Unity.

Unity.Pipeline.IlInterpreter.asmdef declared overrideReferences: false with precompiledReferences: [], so the assembly could only consume auto-referenced plugins and therefore never received a reference to System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.

The same filename was also present at Library/PackageCache/com.unity.pipeline@9bb4172c603c/Runtime/Plugins/CodeAnalysis/System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.dll (4.0.4.0 vs livekit's 6.0.0.0). Run 1 logged Unity's duplicate resolution choosing livekit's copy; with the duplicate present neither copy ended up on the IlInterpreter reference line.

Library/PackageCache/.../Unity.Pipeline.IlInterpreter.rsp in this worktree listed Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.dll / Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.dll and omitted System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.dll, whereas the already-built main checkout's rsp lists exactly three PackageCache plugins: System.Collections.Immutable.dll, System.Reflection.Metadata.dll and System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.dll. Unity.Pipeline.IlInterpreter.dll exists in the main checkout's Library/ScriptAssemblies (built 2026-09-08 23:48) but was absent from this worktree, because this worktree's Library was cloned from the main checkout without a compiled IlInterpreter and had to compile the experimental package from scratch.
action: Moved the duplicate plugin DLL and its .meta out of Library/PackageCache/com.unity.pipeline@9bb4172c603c/Runtime/Plugins/CodeAnalysis/ into the session scratchpad.

Set Unity.Pipeline.IlInterpreter.asmdef to overrideReferences: true with precompiledReferences listing exactly the three DLLs the working main-checkout rsp resolves, so the assembly names the reference explicitly instead of relying on auto-reference.
Deleted Library/Bee and Library/ScriptAssemblies so Bee could not reuse the stale rsp that had been generated under the ambiguous duplicate resolution.
environmentRemediation.scopeNote: All three edits are inside Library/, which is gitignored build state - not a repository path. No tracked file outside the declared write scope was modified. Copies of the original DLL, .meta and .asmdef are in the backup path above.
environmentRemediation.notCausedByCandidate: The candidate touched only Packages/com.xrlab.chooguard.foundation/Multiplayer/Runtime/NetworkFieldRuntime.cs and a new PlayMode test file. Library/ScriptAssemblies at 2026-09-14T17:36 (run 1) already contained ChooGuard.Foundation.Multiplayer.dll carrying RouteDisplayState/ProjectRoute/SyntheticBanner and ChooGuard.Foundation.Multiplayer.PlayModeTests.dll carrying FMP11aRouteProjectionTests and all five test methods, i.e. the candidate compiled cleanly on the first attempt while the unrelated experimental package failed.
environmentRemediation.requiresReview: A reviewer should confirm that the correct durable fix is a project-level one (the precompiledReferences entry belongs in the package's own asmdef upstream, or the unreferenced duplicate DLL should not be shipped) rather than the local Library/ patch recorded here. The local patch is environment remediation for this run only and is not part of the candidate commit.

limits: Portal/id counts come from the authored profile; no region or portal ID was invented. 13 regions and 12 portals are enumerated from the file, not asserted from memory.
The portal graph is a tree (13 nodes, 12 bridge edges): a closed edge strands its far side and no bypass exists. The implementation and tests never invent a detour.

Three portals have an empty LinkedDoorEntityIds list (forecourt_eurasia--underground_connector, rail_terminal_public--underground_connector, underground_shopping_passage--metro_concourse). ConnectedWorldRuntime.ProjectPortals computes Open as All(active) over an empty set, which is vacuously true, so those three can never be closed by equipment state. Their blocked-route coverage is exercised only through a synthetic closure injected into the observed view, and is labelled as such.

The PlayMode test assembly (ChooGuard.Foundation.Multiplayer.PlayModeTests) does not reference ChooGuard.Foundation.Multiplayer.Editor, so scenes are NOT built and ConnectedWorldRuntime.Synchronize/scene loading is not exercised. The projection is tested as a pure function over the authored profile.
Assets/CHOOguardGenerated/ConnectedWorld/ is absent, so the 14 authored scenes do not exist locally.

Run 3 required a local, gitignored Library/ remediation to the experimental com.unity.pipeline package before any PlayMode test could execute at all. Two earlier attempts produced no XML. The candidate code compiled cleanly in every attempt; the blocker was an unrelated package reference, documented under environmentRemediation.
docs/evidence/foundation/proposed/FMP-11a-route-ui.json is the only record committed here; the PlayMode XML/log and the test run record live outside the repository under the session scratchpad.

Unity generated Packages/com.xrlab.chooguard.foundation/Multiplayer/Tests/PlayMode/FMP11aRouteProjectionTests.cs.meta as an Editor-side asset database artefact; it is outside the declared 3-path write scope and is reported, not hidden.

Unity also generated Assets/CHOOguardTeam.meta and Assets/CHOOguardTeam/Art.meta (directory .meta files for an already-tracked directory tree). They are outside the declared write scope and were deliberately NOT staged or deleted.
